newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Tens of thousands of Kazakhs return from Mongolia.
newsitem.headline: Tens of thousands of Kazakhs return from Mongolia.

text.p: Tens of thousands of descendants of Kazakhs who fled famine and Soviet collectivisation in the 1930s have returned from neighbouring Mongolia, the Karavan Blitz newspaper said on Thursday.
The daily said more than 60,000 Kazakhs had returned to their homeland since the former Soviet republic gained independence five years ago.
"More than 80 percent of those Kazakhs who have returned will stay," Mongolia's ambassador to Kazakhstan, Gungaadorzh, told the newspaper.
Once one of the world's largest semi-nomadic peoples, the Kazakhs were ordered by late Soviet dictator Josef Stalin to bow to communist doctrine and settle on collective farms.

Many refused and slaughtered their livestock rather than hand them over to the Soviet authorities, while others rode with their herds across the border into neighbouring Mongolia and China. The resulting famine killed hundreds of thousands.

Post-Soviet hardships, however, have made the return for many "Mongolian Kazakhs" a tough one with most unable to find work or a place to live. Obtaining one of Kazakhstan's new sky-blue passports is also a problem.
"To change citizenship you need to complete 15 different documents," said Gungaadorzh. "Many of the returnees live in remote places, some cannot even read."
There are few nomads left in the state of of 16.9 million to roam across an area of arid steppe five times the size of France.

But "qyz quu", a reckless chase on horseback between a boy and girl, remains a popular spectacle. If the boy catches the girl, he wins a kiss -- if the girl catches the boy she gets to thrash him with her riding crop.
